topic: The Riemann Zeta Function: Bridging Arithmetic and Geometry
target_audience: Undergraduate STEM students with a foundation in Calculus

sections.title: Prerequisites: The Harmonic Series and Convergence
lecture_lines: Consider the infinite series 1/n to the s.
It converges precisely when s is greater than 1.
Think of this like Zeno’s paradox in reverse.
animations: Highlight the terms, demonstrating how they grow smaller.
Show a plot of the sum approaching infinity.
Contrast with a convergent series like 1/n^2.
Highlight the divergence of the harmonic series in #FF4500.

sections.title: Defining the Riemann Zeta Function
lecture_lines: We define the Riemann Zeta function as this sum.
For s greater than 1, the series works perfectly.
Analytic continuation extends this to the complex plane.
animations: Define s as a complex number.

sections.title: The Magic Connection: Euler Product Formula
lecture_lines: Zeta connects directly to the world of primes.
The sum equals an infinite product over primes.
Every integer is built from prime building blocks.
animations: Animate product expansion for the first few primes.
Show terms aligning with the summation formula.
Highlight the equality between sum and product.

sections.title: The Riemann Hypothesis: The Critical Strip
lecture_lines: The critical strip lies between 0 and 1.
The hypothesis concerns where the function equals zero.
All non-trivial zeros lie on line 1/2.
animations: Display the complex plane with the critical strip.
Show the non-trivial zeros lying on this line.

sections.title: Conclusion and Impact
lecture_lines: This remains mathematics' most elusive, unsolved prize.
It holds the key to prime number distribution.
The quest for the proof continues today.
